message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), the melting/freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  

This is a well‑known feature of water’s phase diagram: as the external pressure falls below atmospheric pressure, the solid–liquid equilibrium temperature shifts downward. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about –2 °C (–3.6 °F).
